toegepas.blok: Baie nader aan ons as die Son
toegepas.voor: en ook net soveel kere verder weg
toegepas.na: maar ook net soveel kere verder weg
toegepas.rede_vinder: The two halves pull against each other (bigger, yet further away), so 'maar' carries the reasoning more clearly than 'en'; no comma, as the second half has no subject of its own.
toegepas.fout: 'en ook' joins two facts that pull against each other (bigger, yet further away), so the link that makes the following 'Daarom' work is left flat
toegepas.rede_keurder: Same two facts about the same Sun and Moon; 'maar ook' only makes the counterbalancing explicit, which is the reasoning the next sentence draws on, and protected wording is untouched.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Geen lug en geen vloeibare water
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Craters are holes; 'bly staan' is wooden for them, 'bly behoue' is the natural idiom for something that is not worn away.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'bly staan' is ordinary Afrikaans for something that remains, and 'behoue' is a harder, more formal word for a Grade 4 reader.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Die ruimtepak maak hom heeltemal toe
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'iemand toemaak' usually means covering someone with a blanket; 'omsluit' says the suit closes all round him.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'maak hom heeltemal toe' is clear to a Grade 4 reader in context, while 'omsluit' is a formal word that makes the sentence harder.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Die meeste kraters is gemaak deur rotse
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Die meeste kraters is deur rotse gemaak
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: Afrikaans puts the deur-phrase before the past participle; 'is gemaak deur' follows English word order.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: With a heavy agent phrase carrying its own relative clause, placing it after 'gemaak' is acceptable Afrikaans, and the proposal separates 'rotse' from 'wat uit die ruimte gekom het', so it is a lateral move at best.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Geen lug en geen vloeibare water
laat_vaar_vorige.voor: geen see, rivier of plas water kry
laat_vaar_vorige.na: geen see, rivier of waterplas kry
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The compound 'waterplas' reads more naturally in a list of water bodies than 'plas water'.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'Plas water' is natural Afrikaans and reads well in the list; 'waterplas' is only a different word, not a better one.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: Sonder lug kan 'n mens op die Maan nie asemhaal nie.
laat_vaar_vorige.na: Sonder lug kan 'n mens nie op die Maan asemhaal nie.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: The first 'nie' sits more naturally before the place phrase; the meaning is unchanged.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Both negation positions are natural, and with the Moon already the topic of the paragraph the original order reads well; the move is lateral.

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: pak wat 'n mens se eie lug saamdra
laat_vaar_vorige.na: pak waarin 'n mens sy eie lug saamdra
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: As written the suit itself carries the air; 'waarin ... sy eie lug saamdra' matches the study text, where the person carries the air in the suit.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: The glossary definition is true and clear as it stands (the suit does carry the wearer's air), so a rewording of a [begrip] entry beyond grammar is not warranted and there is no real fault to send to the writer.

laat_vaar_vorige.blok: Hoe die Maan se oppervlak lyk
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: 'rondlê' suggests things lying scattered about carelessly; 'lê oral' says plainly that the dust is everywhere.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: 'lê oral rond' is natural Afrikaans for fine dust spread everywhere; dropping 'rond' is a lateral move.
